reviews.review: The Best Mobile Game Type Horror game I've ever played...

An innovative visual novel which perfectly fits for your mobile phone. No, the game works on your PC too and doing that very well, but experience with a phone in your hands in a way better. So better buy in App Store or Google market.

This is a horror game with a couple of screamers and atmospheric sounds, that's why you'd use headphones.

Before the story got clear I was very into it. But then... Everything went bad. I mean, this is total absurd. I facepalmed multiple times before credits. All suspense disappeared after the main plot twist. Didn't see such stupid things for a while. 

Again, you can buy it on mobile apps market for your phone. Because only one strong thing about this game is the experience of using disappeared person's phone. But the other things are bad. The naive story has an awful finale. Actors play mediocre. Some mechanics doesn't work as they are supposed to work. You can skip rare minigames without penalties. Often it doesn't matter that line you're choosing, because characters answer the same. 

Something similar about the story was in "doki literature club". But there it was realized a way better. So, you shouldn't buy  here, 'cause you'll miss the only one positive thing about this game.

Picture this: you find a girl's phone, and her name is Anna. But here's the catch - she's missing, and you're the one holding her phone with all its personal information. Creepy, right?

The story revolves around investigating Anna's disappearance, and as you interact with her friends and family through text messages and phone conversations, the tension keeps building up. The drama feels real, and the game's decision-based mechanics force you to make choices that affect the outcome. The best part is, it's not just a mystery unraveling over time; your main goal is clear - find Anna. But beware, Simulacra is not just about jumpscares; it plays with your senses more subtly, with eerie audio effects that might even make you question reality outside the game.

Though the game is quite engaging, it's not without its flaws. The voice acting feels a bit awkward and scripted, and some audio elements seem unnecessary, primarily existing for the sake of providing a jumpscare. But hey, the recorded videos are well done, especially Anna's personal vlogs.

Playing this game on PC might not be as immersive as on a mobile phone but it holds its merit reguardless. Still, they could've allowed portrait mode like in Downwell to make it even better.

All in all, Simulacra is a decent horror title that excels in subtle horror and decision-based gameplay. It really makes you think about privacy, honesty, and data security, and that's something you don't often get from a horror game. So, if you're up for an unnerving experience that's a bit different from the usual horror games, give Simulacra a try!

Love this game. In the same vein as films like 'Searching', you spend all of your time navigating a device (in this case a phone) in search of a missing person. Simulacra has more a horror tone than 'Searching', but for much of the game's runtime it's only lightly scary, with most of the suspense coming not from supernatural frights but from further unraveling the mystery by feeling like an amateur cybersleuth. 

There are definitely moments where it was frustrating trying to figure out where to go next, but the game generally does a good job of pointing you in the right direction through the use of hints given by the characters in the game. It all feels organic and never too forced. Multiple playthroughs will be needed to see all of the endings, but even just one playthrough will give every player a satisfying experience in the end. 

My few gripes with this game are that the actors aren't really that great in their performances, and for a game that I think is set in the US (at least that seems like the accent everyone is going for), the actor's accents waver quite often. This is obviously not a big budget production, so it's understandable that top shelf talent isn't within reach, but I would say that instead of trying to force a setting, just go with what's available around you. I don't feel that the US setting is necessary to tell this kind of story. I'd also like if there were some way to expedite replays of the game. Yes, if you do a second playthrough you can skip text much more quickly, but I'm thinking of something kinda like Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward. In that title there was a branching path menu you could pull up and jump exactly to the point where the story diverged. That would save so much time replaying up until the point where a critical decision was made. 

Conclusion:

Fun cyberdetective game told through a smartphone. Elements of horror, but nothing too overdone so that non-horror fans couldn't enjoy. Gameplay makes you do a fair amount of thinking, without too much handholding, so you feel a sense of accomplishment when you unearth another clue. Tons of easter eggs are there for those willing to look. Performances are not great here, but the voiced parts are minimal and don't interrupt the flow too often.

I’m really shocked how such a “small” yet “simple” game could be such a banger, it is great, interesting and awesome. Full playthrough took me about 6 hours and it was amazing – the gameplay is very simple, you just go through the found smartphone, but it is so fresh and original that you can’t stop diving deeper into the gameplay and story; the story itself is very catchy and it mediates between a cool (and I mean really cool) horror story and kind of detective, where you need to solve smart, interesting puzzles. But here are the important things: it does not feel like just a solving puzzles, you literally investigating a very strange and creepy case, everything feels so alive and real (characters, surfing through the mail, chatting, etc.) and most important that it creates a strong feeling that the choices matter – crazy plot twists, extreme tension, and the sense of realism; about horror –  it’s just perfect, not very much of it but it is placed at the right moments and always hits at the right time. 
It definitely gives me some cool vibes that are crazy mix between “laptop” horror movies (Open Windows, Unfriend) and oldschool “teenager” horrors series (Tales From The Crypt, Are You Afraid Of The Dark?). One of the best games I’ve played for a long time and definitely a hidden gem. 
Do I recommend this game? Strongly recommend.

SIMULACRA is a game I first saw on YouTube. I said to myself "Hey, I think I'll pick this up and give it a go. It looks good". Now, after buying it and actually playing it... I just cannot recommend it at all. It feels HEAVILY falsely advertised, to me at least due to the second trailer on steam.  Below I will state why these are my thoughts and what drove me to this conclusion.

[h1][b] My thoughts - Cons? [/b][/h1] 
⚫So to start off, the SECOND steam "TRAILER" for this game has really nothing to do with the game. You get no actual scenes like that at all. Yeah, ok... you get S O M E video scenes but it does NOT look like the second trailer in the slightest and it does not say ANYWHERE "Not actual game footage". 
⚫The game is classed as a "Horror/psychological horror" but as you play it... there is NOTHING scary about the game at all. Do not get me wrong, it had a REALLY great start to it but as you play the game gets overshadowed by "relationship issues" and it takes ALL the horror elements out of the game completely. The more in depth you go the more GOOFIER the plot actually is. Greg with his "Fu** you soooooo much" line or even the sarcastic "Sex offender" you have to talk to that CLEARLY shows who he is. Yeah... nothing mid-end of the game was good at all. 
⚫The lack-there-off accessibility options to turn down audio, adjust frames, settings in general, brightness e.t.c is non existent. You are supposed to be on a phone... come on where is the cog wheel to keep us immersed in this like a REAL phone.

[h1][b] My Verdict [/b][/h1] 
I think that there was to much HYPE based around this game due to several BIG streamers playing it (not going to mention names) and it took off as a "good horror experience" because of it. The lack of horror, accessibility options and sublime goofy plot makes this a dull, boring experience that will leave you feeling like this -  "What did I just spend my time playing" "Was it worth it" "Can I get a refund". 

[h1][b] 3/10 - A goofy plot leads to bad horror experience. [/b][/h1]

Okay, so I'm a massive fan of "Sara Is Missing" which is no longer on Steam (presumably for the extreme content) which was one of the first games Kaigan Games released based on this series, I was excited to play this as I didn't realise this game was made from the same developers, I was extremely impressed! The content isn't as extreme as SIM because I think just about anyone can say that it was extremely dark and disturbing, but I think they were trialling how a game like SIM would do, and it was successful!

Enough about SIM, Simulacra is a fantastic game! The jumpscares are timed amazingly, allowing the player to calm before the next one when they least expect it. Unlike some other games when they over exaggerate the scariness. [spoiler] (I won't lie, I jumped massively at the phone reset and Taylor's jumpscare. That was cruel haha) [/spoiler] The characters are comical, [spoiler] Especially Greg with his voice notes LMFAO[/spoiler] They all have their own individual wittiness about them, personalities and not at any point did I feel like they were lack luster, they all contributed their own to the story which I really appreciate as I find a lot of horror games tend to make characters to make the player build up a connection only them to kill them in the middle or nearer towards the end.

The only critique I'd say would be the crashing, don't get me wrong! It happens to a lot of games, but I think more frequent saving should be happening or let the player save their progress manually in case it does happen. It doesn't happen often, but on the odd occasion I've needed to restart the game. Other than that, if you like a scare, thrill and a mystery; This game is for you. Plus, it's super cheap! Try it out!
